selectedPage.title: Cheek Acne Comparison Page
selectedPage.targetIntent: Support users comparing alternatives, formats, or brands before they choose a solution.
selectedPage.primaryCtaGoal: Route high-intent comparison traffic to the best internal product/category destination.

audience.cohort: Young Indian commuters and students comparing options for cheek breakouts.

cta.primaryGoal: Route high-intent comparison traffic to the best internal product/category destination.

inference.notes: Comparison intent needs methodology, criteria, and tradeoff structure.

researchBasis: selected page title, slug, target intent, page type, and strategy category
live SERP, PAA, social/video, competitor-gap, and audience-language research must refine this before final copy
pageStructure.structureUniquenessRationale: comparison_matrix is the starting structure because the selected opportunity signals comparison intent. The adapter must revise the section sequence, decision tools, FAQs, troubleshooting blocks, tables, superiority components, and CTA placement when current-page research shows different sub-intents or gaps, and must not reuse a structure from another page, batch, or historical run.

sections.purpose: First-fold answer, H1, primary CTA, and surrounding CTA microcopy.
sections.notes: State the comparison promise and primary CTA without declaring a winner before evidence. Primary actionable must be visible in the first fold on desktop and mobile.

sections.purpose: Give a short, qualified verdict for the main comparison intent.
sections.notes: Use a qualified verdict, not a universal winner.

sections.purpose: Explain how options are compared and what evidence is allowed.
sections.notes: Include a concise comparison methodology and qualitative labels unless numeric scoring is explicitly requested.

sections.purpose: Define the criteria readers should use before reading the matrix.
sections.notes: Make each criterion actionable and tied to the search intent.

sections.purpose: Compare options side by side against the stated criteria.
sections.notes: Matrix cells must be specific; avoid generic good/better/best language.

sections.purpose: Explain who each option is and is not for.
sections.notes: Spell out tradeoffs by reader need, not just feature lists.

sections.purpose: Author, reviewer, methodology, experience, proof, and brand trust signals.
sections.notes: Include authored-by visibility and page creation or update date.

sections.purpose: Answer likely questions and support FAQ JSON-LD only when FAQ content exists.
sections.notes: Include FAQ schema draft when this section is present.

sections.purpose: Final primary CTA and conversion-oriented closing copy.
sections.notes: Use one primary CTA variant in V1.

sections.purpose: Reference URLs and source metadata used for page claims.

notes: Review top live search results before finalizing page structure.
Use cited source URLs for claims and reference notes.
Generate top 3-5 high-impact in-page images when possible.
Include a separate OG image asset.
Use image briefs only when generation is unavailable or time-bounded by the user.

structure.reason: Standard V1 section order is proposed before full copy is drafted.

content.reason: The user should choose tone per page and content depth is treated as a target range.

images.reason: Images should follow brand guidelines and include logo/brand signals only when appropriate.

critical.reason: Comparison pages may mention competitors or external products and require explicit approval before inclusion.
